1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Ledger result: the claim set, description, abstract, and reference-numeral table trace cleanly to the inventor's disclosure (which is reproduced verbatim as the single USER passage in conversation.md). Every claim limitation - split semicircular frame halves with hinge and releasable latch, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads, segmented cam ring retained in an annular guide with one segment per half, complementary coupling faces at both ends coupling the segments on closure, followers in oblique slots producing synchronized inward travel, wedge on a ring drive face, latch first/over-center positions, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin against a fixed edge of the latch housing reporting compression and not diameter, carriage return springs, optional mounting boss carrying a sensor/tool/conduit outside the annular guide, and the install/remove method - maps to an exact affirmative sentence in the disclosure. The renaming of the disclosure's "complementary drive faces" (segment-to-segment) to "complementary coupling faces," with "ring drive face" reserved for the wedge-driven face, is a supported disambiguation and is used consistently in claims, description, abstract, briefs, and numerals.md. All 26 numerals are single-meaning, all appear on at least one figure, and section line 3-3 carries the same designation in FIG. 1's brief, FIG. 3's brief, the Brief Description, and the detailed description. No drafting notes, placeholders, or open questions remain in the application text, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" broadening was added to justify a renderer choice. I checked the projection geometry of every view and confirm the view-side and left/right assignments in FIG. 2, FIG. 4, and FIG. 6 are mutually consistent with FIG. 1 (FIG. 4's right band = first cam ring segment and the handle leaning toward the first frame half are both correct for a view from the opposite side).
4	
5	Four defects remain, all in the figure briefs.
6	
7	(1) Critical, unsupported geometry: FIG-3.md affirmatively makes the oblique slot a blind pocket - "it is not shown breaking out at the right face." The disclosure says only "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring," with nothing about the slot's depth or whether it passes through the ring. This is exactly the kind of depth/boundary statement about a functional slot that is substantive even under a schematic label.
8	
9	(2) Major, internal inconsistency arising from the same sentence: FIG-3.md establishes that the view's right is the axial side from which FIG. 1 is viewed, and puts the slot opening in the ring's left face only. FIG-2.md is viewed "from the same side as FIG. 1" and shows all three slots as openings visible in the ring face ("the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it"). The two briefs therefore disagree about whether the slots are visible from the FIG. 1 side. FIG-3.md also contradicts itself, since its own schematic list calls out "the way the oblique slot 34 appears as an opening through the segmented cam ring 20."
10	
11	(3) Critical, unsupported assignment plus self-contradiction: FIG-4.md places the ring drive face 36 on a named segment - "the exposed end region of the left band presents the ring drive face 36," the left band having just been identified as the second cam ring segment 24 - in the same sentence that says "which segment carries it, its radial side, slant and extent are not specified," and after a schematic list that includes "which part of the ring carries it." The disclosure says only "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring" and never says which segment or frame half receives the drive input. FIG-2.md leaves the carrier unspecified, so a render of FIG. 2 could also place the face on the other segment, producing a figure-to-figure conflict.
12	
13	(4) Major, cross-figure geometric conflict at the latch-end joint: FIG-4.md requires the band end regions to be open radially outward so the latch housing cavity "opens downward over the exposed band end regions" and the wedge can descend onto the ring drive face. FIG-6.md depicts the same joint with continuous frame material radially outward of both segments ("a further band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and the break line at its right," repeated for the lower body) and with both the frame end faces and the segment end faces abutting at the parting line, leaving no path by which the wedge could reach the ring.
14	
15	Note on scope: I did not assess patentability, and I did not inspect any rendered image. Consistent with the brief, no prior-art search was run and the art in prior_art/ may be incomplete; Background characterizations were not traced here and are left to the later citation review.
16	
17	## Mechanical checks that did not pass
18	
19	- **Source fidelity is clean before rendering** (fail): Ledger result: the claim set, description, abstract, and reference-numeral table trace cleanly to the inventor's disclosure (which is reproduced verbatim as the single USER passage in conversation.md). The renaming of the disclosure's "complementary drive faces" (segment-to-segment) to "complementary coupling faces," with "ring drive face" reserved for the wedge-driven face, is a supported disambiguation and is used consistently in claims, description, abstract, briefs, and numerals.md. All 26 numerals are single-meaning, all appear on at least one figure, and section line 3-3 carries the same designation in FIG. 1's brief, FIG. 3's brief, the Brief Description, and the detailed description. No drafting notes, placeholders, or open questions remain in the application text, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" broadening was added to justify a renderer choice. I checked the projection geometry of every view and confirm the view-side and left/right assignments in FIG. 2, FIG. 4, and FIG. 6 are mutually consistent with FIG. 1 (FIG. 4's right band = first cam ring segment and the handle leaning toward the first frame half are both correct for a view from the opposite side).
20	
21	Four defects rema
22	  - FIG. 3 brief asserts the oblique slot is a blind pocket that does not pass through the cam ring
23	  - FIG. 4 brief assigns the ring drive face to a named cam ring segment while simultaneously stating that the carrier is not specified
24	  - FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 disagree on which face of the cam ring the oblique slots open in, and FIG. 3 contradicts its own schematic note
25	  - FIG. 6 closes off the latch-end joint that FIG. 4 requires to be open for the wedge to reach the ring drive face
26	
27	## Reviewer findings
28	
29	- **[critical] FIG. 3 brief asserts the oblique slot is a blind pocket that does not pass through the cam ring** (figures/FIG-3.md, paragraph beginning "A hatched block is received in the groove") - The brief affirmatively states the depth/boundary of a functional cam slot: the slot opens only in one axial face of the segmented cam ring and stops short of the opposite face. Depth and run-out of a functional cam slot are substantive geometry, not a depiction convention, and the inventor never described the slot's depth, its axial position in the ring, or whether it is a through opening. No affirmative passage in the disclosure or conversation supports a blind slot; the nearest source passage describes only that the follower is received in the slot and that the slot converts rotation into radial travel.
30	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-3.md delete the clause ", and it is not shown breaking out at the right face" and delete "apart from that opening the block is solid and hatched throughout", so the sentence reads: "One rectangular opening is formed through that block, sized to receive the follower 32. That opening is the oblique slot 34, its position in the block shown schematically." Make no other change; the slot then remains a generic opening with no asserted depth.
31	- **[critical] FIG. 4 brief assigns the ring drive face to a named cam ring segment while simultaneously stating that the carrier is not specified** (figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph 3 ("There the exposed end region of the left band presents the ring drive face 36..."), read) - Which of the two cam ring segments carries the wedge-driven face is a substantive circumferential/topological assignment: it determines which frame half receives the latch input into the coupled ring. The inventor never assigned it. The brief also contradicts itself, disclaiming the very fact it states in the same sentence, and FIG-2.md leaves the carrier open, so a render of FIG. 2 could place the face on the other segment and conflict with FIG. 4.
32	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-4.md replace "There the exposed end region of the left band presents the ring drive face 36" with "There the exposed end region of one of the two bands presents the ring drive face 36", and leave the disclaimer and the numeral target ("target the short inclined face where the wedge 52 meets the exposed band end region at the parting line") unchanged. No segment identification is then asserted in either FIG. 2 or FIG. 4.
33	- **[major] FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 disagree on which face of the cam ring the oblique slots open in, and FIG. 3 contradicts its own schematic note** (figures/FIG-2.md paragraphs 5 and 11 versus figures/FIG-3.md paragraphs 3 and 9) - FIG-3.md fixes the view's right as the axial side from which FIG. 1 is viewed, and puts the slot opening in the ring's left face only, i.e. the face turned away from the FIG. 1 viewer. FIG-2.md is expressly viewed from the same side as FIG. 1 and shows the three slots as openings visible in the ring face. Both cannot be true: from the FIG. 1 side the slots would be invisible under the FIG. 3 geometry. FIG-3.md also contradicts itself, because its own schematic list describes the slot as "an opening through the segmented cam ring 20" while its body says the opening does not break out at the far face.
34	  - Suggested fix: Apply the FIG-3.md edit given in the preceding finding (delete "and it is not shown breaking out at the right face" and "apart from that opening the block is solid and hatched throughout", and render the opening as passing through the block). FIG-2.md then needs no change, and FIG-3.md's schematic note "an opening through the segmented cam ring 20" becomes accurate.
35	- **[major] FIG. 6 closes off the latch-end joint that FIG. 4 requires to be open for the wedge to reach the ring drive face** (figures/FIG-6.md paragraphs 7 and 9 versus figures/FIG-4.md paragraphs 5 and 9) - The two briefs depict the same latch-end joint. FIG. 4 requires the cam ring segment end regions to be uncovered on the radially outer side so the latch housing cavity can open down onto them and the wedge can bear on the ring drive face. FIG. 6 shows continuous frame material radially outward of the segment in both bodies over that same region, and shows both the frame end faces and the segment end faces abutting at the parting line, so nothing could reach the ring either radially or circumferentially. As drawn the wedge in FIG. 4 has no access path to the ring in the structure FIG. 6 depicts.
36	  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-6.md delete the two sentences "In the upper body a further band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and the break line at its right. In the lower body also a band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and the break line at its right." and instead run the irregular break line of each body along the radially outer boundary of its channel, so that FIG. 6 makes no assertion about what lies radially outward of the cam ring segments at this joint. Leave paragraph 3's schematic note about "the extent of the break at each body's radially outer side" in place; it already covers this.
37	
38	Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
39	the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

The annular guide 18 of each frame half appears as a channel opening toward the parting line, one in the upper body opening downward and one in the lower body opening upward. Each channel is set back from the left edge of its body, so a band of hatched frame material stands between the channel and that edge, and the wall of the channel on that side, its radially inner side, faces the block lying in the channel. The irregular break line of each body runs along the radially outer boundary of its channel, so the view shows nothing of what lies radially outward of the two blocks at this joint.

A solid block lies in each channel and reaches along it to the end face of its body without passing beyond it. The block in the upper body is the first cam ring segment 22 and the block in the lower body is the second cam ring segment 24. The two blocks are of the same width and stand in line.

At the parting line the end faces of the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 lie against one another where they meet, so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other; the form of those surfaces and the extent of their engagement are shown schematically. Those surfaces in contact are the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

- 10 first frame half: target well inside the hatched band between the channel of the upper body and its left edge.
- 12 second frame half: target well inside the hatched band between the channel of the lower body and its left edge.

- 22 first cam ring segment: target the hatching inside the block in the upper body, away from the parting line.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target the hatching inside the block in the lower body, away from the parting line.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the horizontal contact between the end faces of the two blocks at the parting line.

FIG. 3 no longer makes the oblique slot a blind pocket: it now reads as one rectangular opening formed through the cam ring block, sized to receive the follower 32, with its position schematic, and the clauses stating that the block is otherwise solid throughout and that the opening does not break out at the far face are gone. That single edit also settles the FIG. 2 versus FIG. 3 disagreement, since FIG. 2 shows the three slots opening in the ring face as seen from the FIG. 1 side and a through opening is visible from either side, and it makes FIG. 3's own schematic note about the slot appearing as an opening through the segmented cam ring accurate. FIG. 4 no longer assigns the ring drive face to a named segment: the exposed end region presenting the face is now one of the two bands, so nothing in FIG. 2 or FIG. 4 states which segment carries the wedge-driven face, and the existing disclaimer and the numeral 36 target are unchanged. FIG. 6 no longer closes off the latch-end joint: the two sentences placing frame material between each channel and the break line are replaced by the irregular break line of each body running along the radially outer boundary of its channel, so the view asserts nothing about what lies radially outward of the two segments there, which is what the schematic note about the extent of the break at each body's radially outer side already contemplated. Because the radially outer channel wall is no longer drawn in FIG. 6, the numeral 18 leader was moved to the channel wall on the radially inner side of the block, and the 10 and 12 leaders were made explicit interior targets in their hatched bands so the three do not compete. While editing FIG. 6 its brief crossed the 2800-character limit, so I condensed the hatching sentence, dropped a redundant scope sentence already covered by the body paragraphs, and shortened the coupling-face sentence; FIG. 6 now measures about 2653 characters and FIG. 4 about 2642, both with margin. Every numeral listed on each sheet is still shown and named on that sheet.
reasoning: The slot fix and the FIG. 2 versus FIG. 3 conflict were one defect with two symptoms, so I made one change. A slot stated to stop short of the far face is a different part from a slot the inventor described only as receiving a follower, and it also hid the slots from the FIG. 1 viewer that FIG. 2 shows them to. Making the opening pass through the block removes the untraced depth statement and closes the cross-figure disagreement without touching FIG. 2.

For the drive face carrier I took the option that leaves the question open in both views rather than harmonizing FIG. 2 to FIG. 4. Which segment receives the latch input determines which frame half the drive enters, and the disclosure never says, so FIG. 4 now says one of the two bands and stops there. That also removes the self-contradiction of naming the carrier and disclaiming it in the same sentence.

At the latch-end joint I changed FIG. 6 rather than FIG. 4 because FIG. 4 needs a path for the wedge to reach the disclosed drive face, while FIG. 6 exists to show the coupling faces. Running the break line along the radially outer boundary of each channel makes FIG. 6 silent about that region instead of contradicting it, and silence is the honest position since the disclosure describes only that the ring is retained in the annular guide.

That silence cost the annular guide its old leader target, which pointed at the radially outer channel wall that is now inside the break. I moved numeral 18 to the radially inner channel wall, which the brief now describes positively, and tightened 10 and 12 to explicit interior targets in their bands so that three leaders in the same neighbourhood remain separable.

The length overrun was a consequence of my own FIG. 6 edit, so I paid for it inside the same file: the redundant sentence limiting the view was dropped because the body paragraphs already fix what appears, the hatching sentence was compressed without losing the requirement that each cut element differ from its neighbours, and the coupling-face sentence lost the upper and lower qualifiers that the parting line already implies.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

# Previous review - verdict: fail

Ledger scope: I traced every limitation of claims 1-15, all 21 reference numerals in draft/numerals.md, and every structure, relationship, result, position, connection, operating condition and variant in draft/04 through draft/10 and in the six figure briefs, to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (identical to the single USER passage in input/conversation.md). Formalities (title, applicant/inventor, "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support statements) match input/brief.md, which is the only authority used for those items.

Supported core chain (all quoted from the disclosure): two semicircular frame halves, hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three radial jaw carriages each sliding in a radial guide and carrying a pivoting concave jaw pad "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; segmented cam ring "retained in an annular guide of the frame", "One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half"; "complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring" on closure; follower per carriage "received in a respective oblique slot"; "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke"; oblique slots giving "synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released"; latch first (holding) and second over-center positions; force-limiting spring stack "between the latch handle and the wedge" absorbing travel "after all jaw pads contact the pipe"; indicator pin moving "relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing" at "a predetermined compression range" and reporting loading, not diameter; the install/remove sequence; and the optional "mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit" that "does not participate in jaw synchronization". Claim 10's assembly (clamp + boss + equipment) and claims 13-15's method map onto those same passages; dependent claims 2-9, 11-12 and 14-15 each restate a disclosed sentence rather than adding matter. I found no untraced limitation, numeral, material, count, proportion, angle or operating condition, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative anywhere in draft/ or figures/.

Functional-surface geometry check: the briefs' substantive geometry statements are each traceable to disclosed function rather than to renderer invention - the oblique slot having one end nearer the inner boundary and one nearer the outer, and all three slots alike and tilted the same way, follow from "translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; the follower contacting the slot sides follows from "follower received in a respective oblique slot"; the drive face lying at the latch end and inclined to the wedge's advance follows from "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face ... and rotates the coupled ring"; the segment ends reaching to (and not past) each frame half's end face follows from faces that "couple the segments" as the halves close; the boss standing radially outside the groove with no part reaching into it follows from "outside the annular guide" and "does not participate in jaw synchronization". Genuinely undisclosed appearances - hinge and pivot circles, latch block outline, handle attitude and outline, housing and cavity form, groove proportions and opening direction, slot positions and tilt sense, spring symbol, break extent, boss and equipment outlines, and the 1/2 distribution of the three carriages between the halves - are each expressly tagged "shown schematically" or "not specified" inside the brief only. No convention leaked into the application text: draft/07 and draft/08 contain no "by way of example", no "any closed outline", and no optional embodiment added to justify a visual choice; draft/08 line 23 keeps the drive face neutral ("presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach").

Internal consistency: numerals are one-to-one with parts and used identically in claims, description, abstract and briefs (26/28 coupling faces vs. 36 ring drive face are consistently distinguished, resolving the source's single term "drive faces"); every numeral in numerals.md appears in at least one brief and in the description. The single section line is designated "3-3" identically in the FIG. 1 source-view brief, the FIG. 3 resulting-view brief, draft/07 and draft/08, with arrows on one side pointing in the direction of sight. I independently checked the view handedness: FIG. 3's stated right (the side FIG. 1 is viewed from), FIG. 4's mirrored left/right band assignment (segment 22 on the right), and FIG. 6's upper-body assignment (half 10 above) are all mutually consistent with FIG. 1's hinge-left/latch-right, half-10-upper layout, and the groove closed on the near axial side in FIG. 3/FIG. 5 is what makes FIG. 6's "wall nearest the viewer broken away" reveal the segments.

One issue found, minor: FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 both declare the radial side of ring drive face 36 unspecified, yet FIG. 4's own geometry (housing cavity above, opening downward, wedge descending onto the exposed band end) fixes the contact as approached from radially outward, so the two briefs could render the same numbered face on opposite sides of the annulus. Fix stated in the finding harmonizes the briefs under one declared convention without adding any geometry to the application text. Prior-art characterizations in draft/05 are unsourced by design and are left to the later citation review; no reference is named there.

## Reviewer findings

- **[minor] FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 leave the radial side of ring drive face 36 unspecified while FIG. 4's wedge geometry fixes it, allowing the same numbered face to be drawn on opposite sides** (figures/FIG-2.md line 13 and numeral list line 23; figures/FIG-4.md lines 7 and 9) - Both briefs describe the same numbered feature, ring drive face 36, and both expressly decline to fix its radial side. FIG. 2 is a plan view along the ring axis, so a renderer following it may place the short inclined face on the inner boundary of the annulus near the right joint. FIG. 4, however, puts the latch housing above the joint with a cavity that 'opens downward over the exposed band end regions' and the wedge descending in that cavity onto the face, which necessarily presents the face for access from radially outward. The result is a latent conflict between two figures for one numeral: face 36 could appear radially inside in FIG. 2 and radially outside in FIG. 4. The same under-specification also leaves FIG. 2 internally ambiguous, since it first says the annulus is 'bounded by one inner circular boundary and one outer circular boundary' and then says 'Apart from that face the boundaries of the annulus are circular', without saying which boundary the face interrupts. This is a figure-specification consistency defect only; the disclosure says nothing about the wedge's direction of advance ('Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke'), and the application text correctly stays neutral (draft/08 line 23: 'The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach'), so no application text needs to change.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-2.md line 13, replace 'which segment carries it, its radial side, its slant and its extent are not specified' with 'which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; it is drawn interrupting the outer boundary of the annulus, on the same side from which the wedge 52 meets it in FIG. 4, that side being a drawing convention only and asserting no radial position.' In figures/FIG-4.md line 7, replace 'which segment carries it, its radial side, slant and extent are not specified' with 'which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; the wedge 52 meets it from radially outward, as in FIG. 2, that side being a drawing convention only and asserting no radial position.' Leave draft/07-drawings.md and draft/08-detailed-description.md unchanged, so the application text continues to say only that the face is 'presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach' and 'lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances'.

Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

# FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring removed from the frame, its two segments drawn in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition, viewed along the ring axis from the same side as FIG. 1, so the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, the positions and tilt of the three slots, and the position, length, form and depth of the ring drive face 36.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area is the segmented cam ring 20, bounded by one inner circular boundary and one outer circular boundary. The region within the inner boundary is open, and between the two boundaries the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments: the upper is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the two segments meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26. At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the annulus width and inclined to the radius at its own position, so one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer. The three are alike and all tilt the same way, so that one direction of rotation of the ring moves all three followers inwardly; the sense of the tilt is shown schematically and is not otherwise specified.

The ring drive face 36 is a short plain straight face of the segmented cam ring 20 in the region of the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its radial side, its slant and its extent are not specified. Apart from that face the boundaries of the annulus are circular.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary in the upper right.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the surfaces meeting at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface near the right joint.

# FIG. 4

Enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end, closed, parts in section, viewed along the frame axis from the side opposite that from which FIG. 1 is viewed. Radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching, the wedge 52, the latch housing 58, each cam ring segment and each frame body at a slant different from that of every other cut element beside it; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the latch housing and its cavity; the position, form, slant and extent of the ring drive face 36 and which part of the ring carries it; the form and extent of its contact with the wedge 52 and the direction in which the wedge 52 advances; the attitude and outline of the latch handle 50; and the drawn path of the force-limiting spring stack 54, shown as one spring symbol.

At the lower left a hatched body holds a hatched arcuate band from the left; at the lower right a second such body holds a like band from the right. The left band is the second cam ring segment 24 and the right band is the first cam ring segment 22. The two bodies meet at a parting line, where the band ends face one another along complementary surfaces, and the channel holding each band opens at that body's end face, so each band end region is exposed at the parting line.

There the exposed end region of one of the two bands presents the ring drive face 36, a short plain straight face drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its radial side, slant and extent are not specified.

Above the parting line a hatched enclosure, the latch housing 58, reaches across both bodies, its left, right and top walls enclosing a cavity that opens downward over the exposed band end regions. A block, the wedge 52, lies in that cavity and meets the ring drive face 36 in a plain inclined contact, so that advance of the wedge 52 moves the band circumferentially.

In the cavity a zigzag line runs upward from the wedge 52 toward the latch handle 50. That line is the force-limiting spring stack 54, lying in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52.

The latch handle 50 stands above the latch housing 58 as a plain straight bar of even width, rising up and to the right from the top wall and leaning past upright, the over-center position. Its mounting is not depicted.

A slender pin, the indicator pin 56, rises from the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects beyond the outer surface of the top wall, that surface being the fixed edge against which the pin is read.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 22 first cam ring segment: target the hatching of the right band.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target the hatching of the left band.
- 36 ring drive face: target the short inclined face where the wedge 52 meets the exposed band end region at the parting line.
- 50 latch handle: target well inside the straight bar.
- 52 wedge: target well inside the block in the cavity.
- 54 force-limiting spring stack: target the zigzag line.
- 56 indicator pin: target the pin above the top wall.
- 58 latch housing: target the hatching of the top wall.

# FIG. 4

Enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end, closed, parts in section, viewed along the frame axis from the side opposite that from which FIG. 1 is viewed. Radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching, the wedge 52, the latch housing 58, each cam ring segment and each frame body at a slant different from that of every other cut element beside it; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the latch housing and its cavity; the position, form, slant and extent of the ring drive face 36 and its carrier; the form and extent of its contact with the wedge 52 and the wedge's direction of advance; the attitude and outline of the latch handle 50; and the drawn path of the force-limiting spring stack 54, shown as one spring symbol.

At the lower left a hatched body holds a hatched arcuate band; at the lower right a second such body holds a like band. The left band is the second cam ring segment 24 and the right band is the first cam ring segment 22. The two bodies meet at a parting line, where the band ends face one another along complementary surfaces, and the channel holding each band opens at that body's end face, so each band end region is exposed at the parting line.

There the exposed end region of one of the two bands presents the ring drive face 36, a short plain straight face drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; the wedge 52 meets it from radially outward, as in FIG. 2, that side being a drawing convention only and asserting no radial position.

Above the parting line a hatched enclosure, the latch housing 58, reaches across both bodies, its left, right and top walls enclosing a cavity that opens downward over the exposed band end regions. A block, the wedge 52, lies in that cavity and meets the ring drive face 36 in a plain inclined contact, so that advance of the wedge 52 moves the band circumferentially.

In the cavity a zigzag line runs upward from the wedge 52 toward the latch handle 50. That line is the force-limiting spring stack 54, lying in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52.

The latch handle 50 stands above the latch housing 58 as a plain straight bar of even width, rising up and to the right from the top wall and leaning past upright, the over-center position. Its mounting is not depicted.

A slender pin, the indicator pin 56, rises from the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects beyond the outer surface of the top wall, that surface being the fixed edge against which the pin is read.

- 22 first cam ring segment: target the hatching of the right band.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target the hatching of the left band.
- 36 ring drive face: target the short inclined face where the wedge 52 meets the exposed band end region at the parting line.
- 50 latch handle: target well inside the straight bar.
- 52 wedge: target well inside the block in the cavity.
- 54 force-limiting spring stack: target the zigzag line.
- 56 indicator pin: target the pin above the top wall.
- 58 latch housing: target the hatching of the top wall.

content.text: The single finding is fixed, with both briefs now under one declared convention.

input.summary: One finding, in the figure briefs only, and it is fixed. FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 both described the same numbered ring drive face 36 while each declined to fix its radial side, so a renderer could have put the face on the inner boundary in FIG. 2 and on the outer side in FIG. 4, where the housing cavity opening downward onto the exposed band end necessarily presents it from radially outward. Both briefs now carry the same declared convention. FIG. 2 says the face is drawn interrupting the outer boundary of the annulus, on the same side from which the wedge meets it in FIG. 4, that side being a drawing convention only and asserting no radial position, which also settles which of the two boundaries the face interrupts and so removes the internal ambiguity against the following sentence that the boundaries are otherwise circular. FIG. 4 says the wedge 52 meets the face from radially outward, as in FIG. 2, with the same convention-only wording. What remains unspecified in both is what the disclosure leaves open: which segment carries the face, its slant, and its extent. In FIG. 2 the cross-reference names the wedge without a numeral, since the wedge is not shown on that sheet and numeral 52 is not in its list; in FIG. 4, where the wedge is shown and listed, the numeral is used. Adding the convention pushed the FIG. 4 brief toward the 2800-character limit, so I trimmed the same file to about 2685 characters by shortening two clauses of the schematic list, dropping the redundant from the left and from the right in the sentence that the next sentence immediately resolves into left band and right band, and replacing an enumeration of the housing walls with its walls, which leaves the later references to the top wall intact. FIG. 2 stands at about 2440 characters. No claim, no sentence of the detailed description, no drawing description, and no entry in draft/numerals.md was touched, and every numeral listed for each sheet is still named on it.
reasoning: The defect was that two sheets disclaimed a fact that one of them silently fixed. FIG. 4 cannot show a wedge descending from a housing cavity onto the ring without presenting the face from radially outward, so leaving the radial side open in both briefs was not neutrality, it was an invitation to draw the same numeral in two places. Declaring one convention in both briefs removes the conflict while keeping the assertion out of the invention.

I kept the disclaimer attached to the convention rather than deleting it, because the disclosure says only that closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring. The briefs now say the drawn side is a drawing convention asserting no radial position, so the sheets agree with each other without either one claiming the ring is built that way.

Fixing the radial side also cured a smaller ambiguity in FIG. 2, which described an inner and an outer circular boundary and then said the boundaries are otherwise circular without saying which one the face interrupts. Naming the outer boundary as the drawn convention closes that gap with no new geometry.

In FIG. 2 I referred to the wedge without its numeral. Numeral 52 is not on that sheet's list because the ring is drawn removed from the frame, and putting a numeral into a brief whose list does not carry it is the kind of mismatch the numeral check catches. The sentence still reads as a cross-reference to FIG. 4.

The length trim came out of the same file the addition went into, and only from wording: the schematic list said which part of the ring carries it where its carrier does the same work, the band sentence said from the left and from the right immediately before the next sentence named the left and right bands, and enumerating the left, right and top walls of the housing was unnecessary once the cavity is described, since the top wall is still referenced by name where the handle and the indicator pin need it.

figures/FIG-4.md: ring drive face 36 now expressly met by the wedge 52 from radially outward, as in FIG. 2, under the same convention-only wording, with segment, slant and extent still unspecified

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and none was added. The independent claims are unchanged and continue to rest on the relationship the inventor calls essential: closing the frame halves is itself what couples the two cam ring segments into one ring through complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and at the latch end, a wedge moved by the latch bears on a ring drive face and turns that coupled ring through a stroke, three oblique slots convert the rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three carriages, and a force-limiting spring stack between the latch handle and the wedge absorbs the handle travel remaining after all three pads land. The Background states the technical problems that combination addresses before they are needed in argument: dividing the drive element with the body surrenders the fixed relationship between the two sides so the clamp settles off center, and a rigid handle drive train forces residual travel into whichever pad touched first while an instrument reading jaw position reports pipe size rather than grip force. This turn harmonized a drawing convention about which side of the ring the drive face is drawn on, which no claim recites, so claim scope is unchanged and the description continues to say only that the face is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge can reach and lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge advances. The drafting brief records that no prior-art search was run, so the art available here may be incomplete and a later search could surface references bearing on these claims.

disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Ledger scope. I traced every limitation of claims 1-15, all 24 rows of draft/numerals.md, and every structure, relationship, result, position, connection, operating condition and variant in draft/04 through draft/10 and in the six figure briefs to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md (which is verbatim identical to the single USER passage in input/conversation.md). Formalities (title, "Not applicable." cross-reference, "Not applicable." government support) match input/brief.md, the only authority used for them. review/previous-qa.md and input/request.md are REVIEWER/SYSTEM context and were used only as context, never as support.
4	
5	Supported core chain, quoted from the disclosure: "first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end"; "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame"; "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame"; "One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half"; "complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring"; "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring"; "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke"; "The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released"; the latch's first holding position and "second over-center position"; "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge"; "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range"; "The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter"; the install and removal sequences; and the optional "mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit" that "does not participate in jaw synchronization". # FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring removed from the frame, its two segments drawn in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition, viewed along the ring axis from the same side as FIG. 1, so the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, the positions and tilt of the three slots, and the position, length, form and depth of the ring drive face 36.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area is the segmented cam ring 20, bounded by one inner circular boundary and one outer circular boundary. The region within the inner boundary is open, and between the two boundaries the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments: the upper is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the two segments meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26. At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the annulus width and inclined to the radius at its own position, so one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer. The three are alike and all tilt the same way, so that one direction of rotation of the ring moves all three followers inwardly; the sense of the tilt is shown schematically and is not otherwise specified.

The ring drive face 36 is a short plain straight face of the segmented cam ring 20 in the region of the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; it is drawn interrupting the outer boundary of the annulus, on the same side from which the wedge meets it in FIG. 4, that side being a drawing convention only and asserting no radial position. Apart from that face the boundaries of the annulus are circular.

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary in the upper right.

- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment.

- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.

input.summary: Both findings shared one root and are fixed by one harmonization in the two briefs that describe ring drive face 36. FIG. 2 now places the face on the end region of one segment at the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially, with which segment carries it, its slant and its extent unspecified, drawn within the width of the annulus with both circular boundaries running unbroken. That removes the statement that the face interrupts the outer boundary, so it no longer conflicts with the same brief's own statement that the ring face between the two boundaries is unbroken except where the slots open in it, and it puts the face in the same location FIG. 4 uses. FIG. 4 now ends the drive-face sentence after the unspecified segment, slant and extent, so the clause fixing the wedge's approach from radially outward is gone, and the housing cavity is now described as open toward the exposed band end regions rather than opening downward over them, which drops the radial direction from the access description while keeping the cavity facing the ring. The self-contradictory disclaimers that trailed both sentences are gone with the sentences they qualified. The FIG. 2 numeral 36 target now reads as the short inclined face on the segment end region at the right joint, matching FIG. 4's existing target on that end region, so one numeral now identifies one place in both views; numeral 28 in FIG. 2 still targets the meeting surfaces at that joint and stays distinguishable, since 36 is the short inclined face and 28 are the circumferentially facing surfaces where the segment ends meet. What survives in both briefs is only what the disclosed function entails: the face lies at the latch end where the latch-driven wedge can reach it, and it is inclined so that wedge advance turns the ring. No claim, no sentence of the detailed description, no drawing description and no entry in draft/numerals.md changed, so the description continues to say only that the face is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach and lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances. Both edited briefs are within the length limit, FIG. 2 at about 2202 characters and FIG. 4 at about 2545.
reasoning: The two findings were one defect seen twice, so I made one edit rather than two. Once the face is located on the segment end region at the latch-end joint in both briefs, the radial verbalizations have nothing to attach to and the one-numeral-two-places conflict disappears with them.

I chose the location the disclosed function actually entails. The latch drives the wedge at the latch end, and the wedge turns the ring, so a face at the latch end inclined to the wedge's advance follows; which radial side the face occupies and which way the wedge comes at it do not follow from anything the inventor wrote, so both are now absent instead of being asserted and then disclaimed in the same breath.

The disclaimers went out with the assertions rather than being reworded. A sentence that fixes a radial side and then says it asserts no radial position cannot be repaired by better hedging, because the geometry is already in the brief and a renderer will draw it.

Changing the cavity from opening downward over the band ends to being open toward them was the smallest change that keeps the wedge able to reach the disclosed face while removing the radial direction. The cavity still faces the ring, which is what the drawing needs, and the brief no longer says from which side.

The FIG. 2 leader for 36 had to move with the face, and I checked it against the neighbouring numeral rather than just retargeting it: 36 is the short inclined face on the segment end region, 28 are the circumferentially facing surfaces where the two segment ends meet at the same joint, so the two leaders describe different features and remain separable.

No application text was touched because none of it recites the radial side, the approach direction or the boundary the face interrupts. That neutrality in draft/08 is what allowed the entire fix to stay inside figures/.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and none was added. The independent claims are unchanged and continue to rest on the relationship the inventor calls essential: closing the frame halves is itself what couples the two cam ring segments into one ring through complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and at the latch end, a wedge moved by the latch bears on a ring drive face and turns that coupled ring through a stroke, three oblique slots convert the rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three carriages, and a force-limiting spring stack between the latch handle and the wedge absorbs the handle travel remaining after all three pads land. The Background states the technical problems that combination addresses before they are needed in argument: dividing the drive element with the body surrenders the fixed relationship between the two sides so the clamp settles off center, and a rigid handle drive train forces residual travel into whichever pad touched first while an instrument reading jaw position reports pipe size rather than grip force. This turn removed drawing-level statements about the radial side of the drive face and the wedge's approach, neither of which appears in any claim, so claim scope is unchanged. The drafting brief records that no prior-art search was run, so the art available here may be incomplete and a later search could surface references bearing on these claims.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

# FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring removed from the frame, its two segments drawn in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition, viewed along the ring axis from the same side as FIG. 1, so the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, the positions and tilt of the three slots, and the position, length, form and depth of the ring drive face 36.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area is the segmented cam ring 20, bounded by one inner circular boundary and one outer circular boundary. The region within the inner boundary is open, and between the two boundaries the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments: the upper is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the two segments meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26. At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the annulus width and inclined to the radius at its own position, so one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer. The three are alike and all tilt the same way, so that one direction of rotation of the ring moves all three followers inwardly; the sense of the tilt is shown schematically and is not otherwise specified.

The ring drive face 36 is a short plain straight face on the end region of one segment at the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; it is drawn within the width of the annulus, and both circular boundaries of the annulus run unbroken.

# FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring removed from the frame, its two segments drawn in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition, viewed along the ring axis from the same side as FIG. 1, so the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, the positions and tilt of the three slots, and the position, length, form and depth of the ring drive face 36.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area is the segmented cam ring 20, bounded by one inner circular boundary and one outer circular boundary. The region within the inner boundary is open, and between the two boundaries the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments: the upper is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the two segments meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26. At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the annulus width and inclined to the radius at its own position, so one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer. The three are alike and all tilt the same way, so that one direction of rotation of the ring moves all three followers inwardly; the sense of the tilt is shown schematically and is not otherwise specified.

The ring drive face 36 is a short plain straight face formed in the face of the annulus near the latch end of the ring and spaced circumferentially from the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; it is drawn within the width of the annulus, and both circular boundaries of the annulus run unbroken.

# FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring removed from the frame, its two segments drawn in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition, viewed along the ring axis from the same side as FIG. 1, so the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, the positions and tilt of the three slots, and the position, length, form and depth of the ring drive face 36.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area is the segmented cam ring 20, bounded by one inner circular boundary and one outer circular boundary. The region within the inner boundary is open, and between the two boundaries the face of the ring is flat and unbroken except where the three slots open in it.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments: the upper is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the two segments meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26. At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the annulus width and inclined to the radius at its own position, so one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer. The three are alike and all tilt the same way, so that one direction of rotation of the ring moves all three followers inwardly; the sense of the tilt is shown schematically and is not otherwise specified.

The ring drive face 36 is a short plain straight face formed in the face of the annulus near the latch end of the ring and spaced circumferentially from the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially; which segment carries it, its slant and its extent are not specified; it is drawn within the width of the annulus, and both circular boundaries of the annulus run unbroken.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary in the upper right.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the surfaces meeting at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top.
- 36 ring drive face: target the short inclined face in the annulus near the right joint, spaced from the joint.

input.summary: One finding, confined to two figure briefs, and it is fixed. In FIG. 2 the ring drive face 36 is now a short plain straight face formed in the face of the annulus near the latch end of the ring and spaced circumferentially from the right joint, drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially, with the carrying segment, slant and extent unspecified, drawn within the width of the annulus and with both circular boundaries running unbroken. Its leader now targets that short inclined face in the annulus near the right joint, spaced from the joint. In FIG. 4 one of the two bands now presents the face in its face at a position spaced circumferentially from the parting line, with the same unspecified carrier, slant and extent; the clause stating that each band end region is exposed at the parting line is deleted, so the fifth paragraph ends with the channel opening at the body's end face; the latch housing cavity is now open toward the band carrying the ring drive face 36 rather than toward exposed band end regions; and its leader now targets the short inclined face where the wedge 52 meets the band, spaced from the parting line. The result is that the latch-end segment ends carry only the coupling function that FIG. 6 depicts as complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28, so no segment end does double duty and numerals 28 and 36 no longer occupy the same region in FIG. 2. I also harmonized one sentence in FIG. 2 that had become internally inconsistent with the relocated face: the statement that the ring face between the two boundaries is flat and unbroken now excepts both the three slots and the place where the ring drive face 36 is formed. What remains in both briefs is only what the disclosed function entails, a face at the latch end of the ring that the latch-driven wedge can reach, inclined so that the wedge's advance turns the ring. No claim, no sentence of the detailed description, no drawing description, no Abstract text and no entry in draft/numerals.md changed, and both briefs remain within the length limit, FIG. 2 at about 2310 characters and FIG. 4 at about 2533.
reasoning: The defect was that the briefs had made one surface do two jobs. FIG. 6 depicts the latch-end segment ends as the complementary coupling faces that transmit circumferential force between segments, and the disclosure assigns those ends only that coupling role, so putting the wedge-driven face on the same ends invented both a location and a second function. Moving the face into the annulus, spaced from the joint, gives each numeral its own surface again.

I kept the two things the disclosed function does entail and dropped everything else. A latch-driven wedge acting at the latch end means the face is near the latch end, and a wedge that turns the ring means the face is inclined; the circumferential end position, the parting-line contact topology and the exposure of the band ends were all inferences the drawing had made on its own.

The cavity description had to move with the face, otherwise the housing would have been opening toward a region no longer carrying the face. Saying the cavity is open toward the band carrying the ring drive face keeps the wedge able to reach it without reintroducing a radial side or an approach direction, both of which earlier passes removed.

Deleting the exposed-band-end clause in the fifth paragraph mattered as much as the drive-face sentence itself, because that clause was the premise the old location rested on. With it gone, FIG. 4 says only that each band sits in a channel that opens at its body's end face, which is what FIG. 6 shows.

Relocating the face made one existing FIG. 2 sentence wrong, so I fixed it rather than leaving a contradiction for the next pass: a face formed in the ring face is an interruption of that face, so the sentence about the ring face being flat and unbroken now excepts the drive face alongside the three slots.

No application text was touched because the description already says only that the face is shown at the latch end of the ring and is presented at a position the wedge can reach. That neutrality is what let the whole fix stay inside figures/, and adding a location to the description to match the drawing would have been the wrong direction of repair.

The independent claims are unchanged and continue to rest on the relationship the inventor calls essential: closing the frame halves is itself what couples the two cam ring segments into one ring through complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and at the latch end, a wedge moved by the latch bears on a ring drive face and turns that coupled ring through a stroke, three oblique slots convert the rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three carriages, and a force-limiting spring stack between the latch handle and the wedge absorbs the handle travel remaining after all three pads land. The Background states the technical problems that combination addresses before they are needed in argument: dividing the drive element with the body surrenders the fixed relationship between the two sides so the clamp settles off center, and a rigid handle drive train forces residual travel into whichever pad touched first while an instrument reading jaw position reports pipe size rather than grip force. This turn moved a drawing-level location for the drive face and removed an asserted exposure of the segment ends, neither of which appears in any claim, so claim scope is unchanged. The drafting brief records that no prior-art search was run, so the art available here may be incomplete and a later search could surface references bearing on these claims.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Ledger scope: the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (identical in substance to input/disclosure.md) is the sole invention authority; input/brief.md supplied the title, applicant/inventor (Nimo Rotem), "no priority claim", and "no federally sponsored research", all of which match 01-title.md, 02-cross-reference.md and 03-government-support.md.
4	
5	Supported and traced (no finding): split clamp 100 with semicircular halves 10/12, hinge 14 at one end, releasable latch 16 at the other; frame annular in the closed condition; three jaw carriages 30 distributed around the closed frame, each sliding in a radial guide 38 and carrying a pivoting concave jaw pad 40 that seats without a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter; segmented cam ring 20 retained in annular guide 18 with one segment 22/24 per half; complementary coupling faces 26/28 at the hinge and latch ends brought into engagement by closing the halves so the segments transmit circumferential force and move/rotate as one coupled ring, and separated when the halves are swung apart; follower 32 on each carriage in a respective oblique slot 34 inclined to the radial direction, translating ring rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three carriages; wedge 52 driven by the latch against a ring drive face 36 to rotate the coupled ring through a limited stroke; carriage return springs 44 biasing each carriage outward on release; latch first (holding) and second over-center positions; force-limiting spring stack 54 between latch handle 50 and wedge absorbing residual handle travel instead of over-driving one jaw; indicator pin 56 moving relative to a fixed edge of latch housing 58 at a predetermined compression range and reporting loading, not diameter; optional mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide carrying equipment 80 (sensor, tool, or conduit) and not participating in synchronization; and the disclosed install/remove sequence, which claims 13-15 and the Operation section follow step for step. Every claim limitation in claims 1-15 traces to that passage; claims 5, 9 and the "reusable/next installation" statements trace to "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter" and "reusable". Background paragraphs are prior-art characterizations and are exempt.
6	
7	Internal consistency checks passed: all 24 numerals in numerals.md are used, each denotes exactly one part, and every numeral appears in at least one figure brief; claims, Summary, Abstract and Detailed Description use the same relationships and the same terms (the source's two distinct uses of "drive face" are consistently disambiguated as "complementary coupling faces 26/28" versus "ring drive face 36"); the only named section line, 3-3, carries the same designation in the FIG. 1 brief (numeral 3 at each arrow end), the FIG. 3 brief, and 07-drawings.md; the FIG. 3 arrow direction, the "view's right = FIG. 1 viewer's side" statement, the groove-mouth/follower path, and FIG. 6's "near wall broken away" all resolve consistently; FIG. 4's left/right segment assignment and handle lean are reconcilable with FIG. 1 and FIG. 6; 07-drawings.md matches each brief; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains in any draft/ file.
8	
9	Findings: three critical disclosure_fidelity items, all on one functional surface - the ring drive face 36. The source says only that "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." It never gives that face an angle, a slant relative to the wedge's travel, a circumferential position relative to the segment joint, or a contact form. The draft nevertheless verbalizes (a) in the application text, that the face "lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge 52 advances"; (b) in the FIG. 2 brief, that it is "drawn inclined so that a wedge bearing on it can move the ring circumferentially" and is "spaced circumferentially from the right joint"; and (c) in the FIG. 4 brief, the same inclination plus "meets the ring drive face 36 in a plain inclined contact" and spacing from the parting line. Under the functional-surface rule, angle/taper, circumferential end position, and contact topology are substantive even where the brief labels the geometry schematic, and the "not specified" hedges in the same sentences do not cure the verbalized relationships. Note that the wedge's own inclined face is inherent in the disclosed term "wedge" and should be retained; only the assertions about the ring's face and the wedge-to-ring contact form need to come out. A minimally specific plain face on the ring at the latch end may remain as a depiction convention, since the source affirmatively discloses that the wedge bears on a drive face of the ring there.
10	
11	No other untraced structure, relationship, result, material, shape, position, connection, operating condition, or variant was found. Radial-end offsets of the oblique slots, the common tilt sense of the three slots, the frame-bore-to-pipe clearance, the guide-to-guide meeting at the groove mouth, the flush segment ends at the parting line, the boss standing clear of the guide, and the "fixed edge" being the housing wall the pin emerges through are each entailed by disclosed structure or function.

19	  - FIG. 2 brief verbalizes an undisclosed slant and an undisclosed circumferential position for the ring drive face 36
